item.description: From higher-yield orchards to modern irrigation and digital farming, Uzbekistan is changing how its farms operate. Business Line examines the investment and support behind these developments, and the challenge of increasing exports while securing domestic food supplies.

item.title: Euronews: How AI glasses are changing the way people communicate
item.description: AI glasses, more than half of which are made in China, are moving from gadget to everyday tool for travellers and people with hearing loss, as makers hope they will one day replace smartphones.

item.title: Euronews: Qatar sees 'progress' in US-Iran talks after White House meeting
item.description: A day after Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met Trump at the White House, a Qatari foreign ministry spokesman said both sides were making positive statements about a diplomatic solution but that “we cannot say how close or how far away an agreement is.”

item.title: Euronews: ‘Scared to death of those stairs’: Addressing the fear of falling among older adults
item.description: Falls pose a significant health risk for older adults, and the likelihood and severity of fall-related injuries increase with age. Yet many people remain unaware of the factors that contribute to falls, including anxiety, hearing loss and mobility problems.

item.title: Euronews: Infineon says AI data centre boom to persist despite growing backlash
item.description: Infineon expects soaring demand for chips powering AI infrastructure to sustain growth, despite mounting concerns over the environmental and economic costs of data centre expansion.

item.title: Euronews: Denmark pledges €643 million in military aid as Zelenskyy meets Nordic leaders
item.description: The Copenhagen talks coincided with the start of US-mediated negotiations between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: Euronews: Vodafone suffers huge net loss on Germany hit but raises full-year outlook
item.description: British mobile phone giant Vodafone on Tuesday posted a huge post-tax loss for its first half, linked primarily to a writedown in Germany, but raised its outlook with total revenue increasing.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: Europe and US agree to review postwar continental security as Ukraine talks begin
item.description: The Abu Dhabi meetings open with an agreement between the U.S. and EU to look at a new security structure for Europe when Russia's war on Ukraine ends.

item.title: Euronews: EU pledges €10 million for Bulgarian Black Sea search, rescue operations
item.description: The EU has pledged €10 million for Bulgaria to bolster search and rescue operations in the Black Sea, which is becoming one of the most dangerous transport routes in the world due to continued drone attacks.

item.title: Euronews: Central Asia's first wind farm with large-scale batteries nears completion in Uzbekistan
item.description: Twenty-five of the 26 turbines are already supplying the national grid, while the storage system undergoes safety checks. The €232m investment includes international financing and a 25-year electricity purchase agreement, as large-scale storage installations in Europe more than doubled in 2025.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: US military aircraft pulled from second UK base after ‘Iran threat’
item.description: Bombers were withdrawn from RAF Fairford in October after an Iran-linked security incident.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: Prince Harry slams ‘lawless’ social media’s impact on children
item.description: Duke and Duchess of Sussex visit the European Parliament.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: COP31 : l’UE soutiendra l’objectif d’électrification
item.description: Selon trois diplomates, le bloc serait parvenu à un consensus pour soutenir l'engagement phare du sommet.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: EU to back COP31 electrification target
item.description: Diplomats say the bloc has reached a consensus to support the summit's keynote pledge.

item.title: Euronews: Aerial footage reveals devastation after deadly Bulgaria highway crash
item.description: Drone footage shows the aftermath of a massive pile-up involving dozens of vehicles on a foggy highway near Yambol, Bulgaria, where 11 people were killed and dozens injured, according to state media.

item.title: Euronews: Portugal on alert as storm Charles brings red warnings to Madeira
item.description: The government warns of flooding, falling trees and power cuts, urging people to shelter "during peaks of rain and wind". Forecasts indicate heavy rain with thunder, six-metre waves and gusts up to 130 km/h, with parts of Madeira under red alert.

item.title: Euronews: Five EU countries demand UK pays for electricity market access
item.description: The leaders of Belgium, Germany, Denmark, Luxembourg and the Netherlands want Britain to contribute to EU regional development funds in return for closer energy ties, adding a new hurdle to negotiations ahead of the 20 November summit.

item.title: Euronews: Latest news bulletin | November 10th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 10th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Euronews: EU candidates will not have a say on anti-Orbán safeguards
item.description: Montenegro is the first to test the EU's new safeguards, with member states expected to reach a position as early as next week. But contrary to the other negotiating chapters, Podgorica is finding out that the safeguards, including the possibility of suspending voting rights, are non-negotiable.

item.title: Euronews: Europe must stop 'begging' for seat at Ukraine peace talks, ex-NATO chief warns
item.description: Former NATO boss Anders Fogh Rasumussen warned Europe against merely pleading to part of the US-brokered ceasefire talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, saying that securing a seat at the negotiating table comes through strength, not “begging”.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: EU capitals fail to reach a deal on nicotine taxes
item.description: Despite Ireland warning of no “better, brighter day” to resolve the issue, a deal was out of reach.

item.title: Euronews: European stocks rise as tech rally spreads and oil prices fall
item.description: Stocks rallied on Tuesday, extending a technology-led surge on Wall Street, as investors took advantage of lower prices following last week's rout. Falling oil prices added to the upbeat mood.

item.title: Euronews: Japan to supply Philippine military with coastal radar and drones
item.description: Tokyo says the new equipment will help Manila monitor shipping routes that are also important to Japan.

item.title: Euronews: Donnie Dunagan, the Purple Heart marine who was the original voice of Disney’s Bambi, dies aged 92
item.description: Dunagan was six years old when he voiced the young deer in the classic Disney animated film. He went on to enlist in the Marine Corps and retired as a Major with three Purple Hearts.

item.title: Euronews: At least 11 dead and dozens injured in Bulgarian motorway pile-up
item.description: Drone footage shows cars crushed between lorries in thick fog near Yambol, and the road has been closed in both directions in an incident involving over 50 vehicles.

item.title: Euronews: Spain clears Ceuta port migrant camp as 300 return to Morocco
item.description: Around 5,800 people are still living in emergency facilities set up after mass arrivals in the territory at the end of July.

item.title: Euronews: Trump says Iran war ‘effectively over’ as Tehran denies planned talks
item.description: Speaking after meeting Qatar’s prime minister, a key mediator, Trump said further strikes were “quite unlikely” but that the US was “locked and loaded”. Meanwhile, Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei told Washington to stop “manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks”.

item.title: Euronews: Inside the Japanese programme using school committees and remedial classes to improve learning in Madagascar
item.description: A programme developed by the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) is tackling low literacy and school dropout in Madagascar by giving parents and communities a direct say in how schools are run.

item.title: Euronews: Prince Harry and Meghan back EU campaign against online bullying
item.description: The Duke of Sussex, in Brussels, praised the EU Kids Act, the proposed law regulating how children use online services, while the Duchess stayed silent following her father’s arrest over alleged possession of child sexual abuse material.

item.title: Euronews: Macron wants AI banned wherever it threatens children
item.description: The French president made the comments as the country draws up a charter to protect its citizens from threats posed by artificial intelligence.

item.title: Euronews: Trump vows to back Pete Hegseth as Republican lawmaker pushes impeachment vote
item.description: Republican Congressman Thomas Massie is seeking to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging military action against Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorisation.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: EU offers cash for Black Sea attack response
item.description: Washington is pursuing a diplomatic effort on safe passage, weighing proposals from Turkey and India.

item.title: Euronews: More computing power, more jobs? Denmark boosts its AI supercomputer
item.description: The 500 million DKK (€67 million) investment in Denmark’s AI supercomputer could help create businesses and jobs and enable public institutions to use AI securely, according to Tuesday’s announcement.
